page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.32-128 is a compute-oriented virtual machine instance built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9J45 processor operating at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The hardware configuration provides 32 dedicated physical cores supporting 64 vCPUs via two threads per core. System memory totals 128.0 GB, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio tailored for parallel execution without surplus memory overhead.

The instance does not include integrated local storage or hardware accelerators, featuring zero GPUs and requiring attached network block volumes for persistent data operations. The omission of local NVMe drives shifts storage throughput and latency expectations entirely to network-attached block infrastructure. Network capabilities include one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Because of the 1:2 vCPU-to-memory configuration and dedicated core model, the VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.32-128 offers efficient computational density for CPU-heavy tasks. The architectural profile is suited for workloads such as distributed compilation, continuous integration and deployment pipelines, batch processing, and horizontally scaled web serving fleets.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.32-128 is a flexible compute instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor running at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 32 dedicated physical cores and 64 vCPUs through simultaneous multithreading, paired with 128.0 GB of system memory at a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The configuration features no local storage and no GPU accelerators, using network-attached volumes for data persistence. One complimentary public IPv4 address is included. Designed with a compute-biased memory-to-core balance, the instance delivers high multi-core capacity while eliminating the cost overhead of excess RAM. It is suited for parallel, CPU-bound workloads such as continuous integration pipelines, batch data processing, software compilation, and scalable web application backends.
